name: Hopline
tagline: Chat with everyone around you when there's no signal
description:
Hopline is group chat for places with no mobile signal and no WiFi: treks, camps, festivals, fairs, rallies, power cuts.

Phones link to each other directly over Bluetooth and WiFi, and every phone passes messages along for the others. A message can travel down a whole line of hikers or across a packed ground, far beyond the reach of any single phone. No internet, no account, no server, no hotspot to set up.

One person starts a group and gets a 3-word code like "tiger river lamp". Everyone else types the three words or scans the QR. Then it's one group chat that looks and feels like the chat apps you already know, with private chats a tap away. Walk out of range and back, and the chat catches up by itself.

The ticks never lie: a clock while it waits for a phone in range, one tick when it's on its way, two ticks when phones confirm. Tap your own message to see exactly who has it, by name.

Built for a few friends or a crowd: in a small group every phone confirms every message; in a gathering of hundreds or thousands the phones automatically stop chattering about receipts and slow their "I'm here" beacons, so the radios carry your words instead of overhead.

If anyone in the group has internet, everyone can use a sliver of it: read a web page as plain text, or send an SMS/email home through the friend's phone — the answer hops back to the whole group.

Android 8+ with Google Play services. Each hop is Bluetooth range (about 20-40 m in the open). Android only; no end-to-end encryption; text only on purpose. Install it on every phone before you need it.
